case_title: West Nile meningoencephalitis with basal ganglia and thalamic MRI abnormalities and long-term sequelae
source_title: The natural history of West Nile virus infection presenting with West Nile virus meningoencephalitis in a man with a prolonged illness: a case report

confirmatory_evidence: West Nile IgM titer positive in acute and convalescent phase
Aseptic CSF pleocytosis with elevated protein
MRI T2 hyperintensity and edema in caudate, lenticular nuclei, basal ganglia, and thalami
EEG diffuse slowing without seizure activity
case_quality.boundary_notes: This is WNV meningoencephalitis with deep gray matter involvement and long-term residual deficits, not isolated viral meningitis.

time_anchor.day0_definition: Emergency presentation with fever, confusion, meningismus, CSF evaluation, and ICU admission

risk_context.source_text_value: History of chronic hepatitis C virus infection.

presentation_summary: 56-year-old man with hypertension and chronic hepatitis C presented after three days of fever, myalgias, headache, decreased appetite, restlessness, and progressive confusion.
Peak temperature was 105.2 F, with neck rigidity, inability to follow commands, stupor, and mild right hemiparesis.
Serum WBC was mildly elevated at 10,400/mm3 with neutrophil predominance.

CSF showed WBC 29/uL with 81% lymphocytes, 15% neutrophils, protein 87 mg/dL, and glucose 63 mg/dL; Gram stain, AFB stain, bacterial meningitis screen, cryptococcal antigen, VDRL, blood cultures, urine cultures, and CSF cultures were negative.
He received broad-spectrum antibiotics and IV acyclovir while HSV, TB, CMV, and WNV testing was pending.
EEG on day 2 showed diffuse slowing without seizure activity.

Brain MRI on day 2 showed enlarged caudate nuclei and increased T2 intensity in caudate, lenticular nuclei, and thalamus; serial MRI improved by day 13, day 21, and six weeks but did not fully normalize.
WNV IgM titer became positive in acute and convalescent phase; at four years he had motor and mental processing speed difficulty and mild residual right hemiparesis.

treatments.dose_or_context: Vancomycin, ceftriaxone, ampicillin, tetracycline, and intravenous acyclovir while diagnostic studies were pending

outcome.neurologic_outcome: Mental status recovered during hospitalization, but MRI did not fully normalize; one year later depression developed, and four years later there were motor and mental processing speed deficits with mild residual right hemiparesis.
outcome.mortality_hazard_relevance: Severe hyperpyrexia, stupor, deep gray encephalitis, and ICU admission increased acute hazard, but he survived with residual disability.

case_boundary_warnings: Deep gray MRI abnormalities are not specific to WNV, but become strong WNND evidence when paired with compatible aseptic meningoencephalitis and positive WNV IgM.
Empiric antibiotics and acyclovir are diagnostic uncertainty bridge therapies, not direct WNV disease-modifying labels.
Long-term depression and processing-speed deficits are preserved as outcome/sequelae, not as presentation-only ranking evidence.
